title: RewriteLab
excerpt: RewriteLab compares reachable rewrites with every equivalent expression in a small grammar. It keeps the complete bounded graph and a shortest proof for every reachable tree. A cheaper expression can fit the size limit but need a larger intermediate tree to reach it.
headings: A shortcut can need a larger detour
Budget barriers: fitting is not reaching
Integer cost weights over one graph

title: RiskLab: static and nested CVaR
excerpt: RiskLab compares static CVaR and nested conditional CVaR on a supplied finite scenario tree. It enumerates every full deterministic policy on that tree and shows terminal probabilities, tail weights and independently replayable certificates. The two objectives can select different policies.
headings: A root-optimal policy can still have a worse continuation

title: RobustLab: exact linear threat-set audits
excerpt: RobustLab computes worst-case margins and attacks for binary linear classifiers. It compares ordinary and robust logistic training, checks exact rational boundaries, and solves attacks inside explicit coordinate bounds. Each audit names its threat set and returns an attack that attains its minimum margin. It uses only Python's standard library.
headings: Box intersection: an optimal witness, not a clipped candidate

title: ScanLab
excerpt: ScanLab compares sequential state updates with associative prefix scans. It returns exact rational states, dependency graphs, arithmetic counts and derivative checks for diagonal and small full-matrix recurrences. A separate floating-point model shows input gating, streaming and rounding failures.

title: ScoreLab
excerpt: ScoreLab enumerates the complete policy-gradient distribution of a supplied finite model at a softmax anchor. It compares full-return and reward-to-go estimators, state-value baselines, and optimal scalar and matrix score controls using exact rational means and covariances.
headings: Matrix score controls and covariance gaps
When the exact value baseline increases variance
Exact rational gradients at a softmax anchor
Why the optimal baseline is not the state value

title: ScratchGPT
excerpt: A small NumPy GPT with three inspectable execution paths: exact training continuation, block recomputation during backward and cached inference that rebuilds when the learned-position window moves.
headings: A restart must preserve the next update
Reuse KV states only while their context stays valid

title: SegmentLab
excerpt: A confident segmentation is not evidence that an event occurred. SegmentLab is a dependency-free Python implementation of exact offline Bayesian Gaussian changepoint inference. It retains the full finite-partition evidence and marginals, not only one best cut list.
headings: Selected results, and what they mean

title: SetGuard: classifier prediction sets with an explicit coverage boundary
excerpt: A dependency-free Python CLI/API for calibration labels plus classifier probabilities, versioned JSON artifacts and unlabeled prediction sets. This is a standard split-conformal method, not a new algorithm.
headings: SetGuard: classifier prediction sets with an explicit coverage boundary
v0.2: every inclusion has a witness

title: ShapleyLab: inspect the game behind feature credit
excerpt: ShapleyLab computes feature credit from small, declared background-replacement games. Inspect every coalition, hybrid input and marginal contribution in Python or the browser. The Python runtime has no dependencies and needs Python 3.10+; it provides a scalar callback API and a strict JSON CLI. No model training or paid APIs.
headings: ShapleyLab: inspect the game behind feature credit
Counterexamples are part of the demo

title: ShieldLab
excerpt: ShieldLab solves three small protocol-game objectives: stay safe forever, reach a safe goal for the first time, or stay safe while visiting a target infinitely often. These are separate inspectors with different stopping rules.
headings: Safety: a safe next step can still lose
Reach-avoid: safe waiting is not arrival

title: SparseLab: check the fit, not just the coefficients
excerpt: SparseLab fits small LASSO regressions and records every solver sweep. Check the primal objective, dual gap and KKT residuals, then compare with exact-rational active/sign enumeration. The Python runtime has no dependencies. A sparse coefficient vector can be one of many equally good fits, not an identified feature ranking.
headings: SparseLab: check the fit, not just the coefficients

title: SpecLab
excerpt: Exact within-proposal stopping for speculative sampling: a stopped proposal tree, full sequence/count laws, independent full-path replay and an editable BigInt inspector. Keeping a low-confidence stop token preserves the target law; a deliberately wrong censor-and-forget control gives full-sequence TV 1/8. No library accusation, trained LLM or speedup claim.

title: SpectralLab
excerpt: Normalized spectral clustering exposes a choice that a scatter plot can hide: which points are neighbors, and what their connection means. SpectralLab builds the affinity and normalized Laplacian explicitly, retains the eigenspace, normalizes every row and runs manual k-means. NumPy supplies the symmetric eigenvalue solve through LAPACK.
headings: A relaxation is not a discrete optimum

title: sre-toolkit: error budgets, alert rules and incident records
excerpt: A dependency-free Python CLI and library for error-budget math, supplied-sample burn rules, keyword alert triage and incident documents. The tools run on local records; they are not a monitoring service or an incident-response platform.
headings: sre-toolkit: error budgets, alert rules and incident records

title: StableLab: inspect stable models and module replacements
excerpt: StableLab checks small, supplied normal logic programs in three ways: enumerate stable models, compare modules under added rules, or compare them under fact inputs only. It runs offline without a solver dependency.
headings: StableLab: inspect stable models and module replacements
Stable models: support is not grounding
Strong equivalence: replacement under rule contexts
Uniform equivalence: replacement under fact inputs

title: STNLab: temporal constraints, bounds and repairs
excerpt: STNLab checks small temporal networks: whether their constraints fit together, which time differences they imply, what one extra constraint changes, and which edge removals repair a conflict. Each answer comes with a path, a complete schedule or a negative cycle that can be checked independently.
headings: STNLab: temporal constraints, bounds and repairs

title: STRIPSLab: real plans, relaxed plans and action availability
excerpt: STRIPSLab compares real and delete-relaxed plans in a fully disclosed state space: zero to six Boolean facts, positive initial/goal/precondition sets, and at most eight positional unit-cost actions. Each action has add and delete sets. The real successor deletes then adds; the relaxed successor only adds. Facts absent from a state are false, not unknown.
headings: STRIPSLab: real plans, relaxed plans and action availability
Action availability: used does not mean necessary

title: StructGate: local masks and future acceptance
excerpt: StructGate compares local viability masking with exact finite-horizon conditioning for a supplied first-order source and total DFA. The default word 01 has source probability 1/20, viability-mask probability 1/2 and global conditional probability 1/10. Inspect every future mass, transition, selected-word prefix and forward marginal.
headings: StructGate: local masks and future acceptance
Original model masking and trie conditioning

title: SubgameLab: a threat is not a credible plan
excerpt: Root stability is not continuation credibility. This exact finite sequential multiagent workbench separates root one-node stability, full-player pure Nash equilibrium and subgame perfection, retaining complete contingent plans rather than only observed outcomes.
headings: SubgameLab: a threat is not a credible plan
An empty threat survives root Nash
One-node root stability can miss a joint change
Zero reach does not erase the subgame

title: SubmodLab: a guarantee is not an optimum
excerpt: Subset selection is often described as picking the most useful or diverse data. Those descriptions can hide the objective, overlap, theorem assumptions and the gap between a greedy solution and an exact optimum. SubmodLab makes each finite decision inspectable without claiming supplied similarities have learned meaning.
headings: SubmodLab: a guarantee is not an optimum
Why the certificate uses k, not the remaining budget
Exact expectation and deterministic cardinality rounding
